pos.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: the 1872-89 combination identity (Robinson 1920 'Combination was the chief characteristic of the Queen's Park play'; SFHG and scotsfootballworldwide on passing combination) values keeping the ball and sees possession as protection, but it does not treat having the ball as the same as dominating the game.

pro.personaBrief: Verified build-up evidence (SFHG passing-game page, Scotsman 1872 account, The Field quoted via Wikipedia) points to combination passing with a 'judicious plan of passing', while The Field also mentions long kicks; the team plays out with short passes, uses the long ball when a forward is free, and prefers to organise before attacking rather than shoot within a few touches.

est.personaBrief: Verified shape evidence (SFHG 1872 page, These Football Times): the 1872 Scotland side was a fixed 2-2-6 box of two full-backs, two half-backs and six forwards, drilled by captain Gardner, so positions are defined; close combination play suggests tight rondo-like combining, while the forwards stayed forward rather than dropping deep, and the winger question has no real referent in a box with no wingers.

lar.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: a 2-2-6 box has six central forwards and no wingers, and the combination side built its attacks through the middle with short passing rather than crossing from the flanks, so central routes and central players are preferred.

blo.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: the 1872 box kept two full-backs and two half-backs behind six forwards, so the team defended from a deep, compact back layer rather than pressing high; it values safety at the back and does not chase the ball in the opponent's half.

mar.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: early Scottish football marked opponents individually and the 1872 defensive layers were assigned players, so the team prefers each defender to pick up an opponent and values the clear responsibility that man-marking brings.

pla.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: the amateur club had no coach and its identity was the combination style; the team keeps its own way of playing and changes little in-game, preparing around its own model rather than the opponent's weaknesses.

res.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: the combination ideal was amateur play valued for its style (Robinson 1920 'combination', Wikipedia on the 1872 Wanderers tie), so how the team plays matters and it is remembered for it; with no stated view, late defensive shifts are not favoured, and away draws are left neutral.

sis.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: the drilled 2-2-6 box and captain-led combination (SFHG, scotsfootballworldwide) make the collective system the source of the team's strength, with everyone playing a role; the team did not rely on free-roaming individual talent.

jog.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: the team's play is described as passing and combination with 'dribble little' (The Field via Wikipedia), so technique and a classic creative player are valued above pace and physicality, and big games are not seen as decided by aerial duels.

bas.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: as an amateur Glasgow club whose entire 1872 national side came from one club (Wikipedia, These Football Times), the team was built from its own local players and valued developing them as much as winning, rather than chasing experienced signings.

lid.personaBrief: General knowledge gap axis: with no coach, the amateur committee and gentlemanly club culture relied on shared discipline and the group's view; the rules apply to everyone, and the team's leadership was collective rather than a coach managing people's feelings.
